subject: humanities
notes: The Scream is a work by the Norwegian artist Edvard Munch.
Munch created the first painted version in 1893.
It shows a figure with its hands pressed to its face, standing by a railing beneath a swirling orange and red sky.
Munch made several versions of the image, including paintings, pastel drawings, and prints.
stem: The student wants to introduce The Scream to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Munch created the first painted version of The Scream in 1893.
choices.B: In addition to the first painted version from 1893, Munch made other versions of the image as paintings, pastel drawings, and prints.
choices.C: The Scream, an 1893 painting by Norwegian artist Edvard Munch, shows a figure pressing its hands to its face beneath a swirling sky.
choices.D: The figure in The Scream presses its hands to its face as it stands by a railing beneath a swirling sky.

explanation.why: Readers who do not know The Scream need to learn what kind of work it is, who made it, and what it shows. Only one choice gives all three: it is an 1893 painting, it is by the Norwegian artist Edvard Munch, and it shows a figure beneath a swirling sky.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It gives a date but refers to "Munch" without explaining who he is, and it never says what the work shows.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It describes the different versions of the image, which assumes the reader already knows the work.
explanation.C: Correct. It identifies the work as a painting, names the artist and his nationality, and describes what it shows.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It describes the image but never says what The Scream is or who created it.
